user_reviews.Name: Sariya S.
user_reviews.Description:
This place is huge and features a beautiful Japanese-style garden. It was super crowded when I visited, likely because it coincided with the Chiang Mai University graduation. The crowd was a mix of teenagers and office workers, so it was quite bustling and not very peaceful. Luckily, my group managed to find a seat just in time!

There is an 80 THB entrance fee, but you can use the ticket as a discount for food and drinks inside.

The prices are standard for a cafe, and everything tasted good. The staff were friendly and provided great service. Since it was so busy, the drinks were served in order, so you might have to wait a bit. Overall, a lovely spot—just be prepared for the crowd on busy days!

user_reviews.Name: Omar El-Naggar
user_reviews.Description: Delicious coffee. I just finished taking my Professional Barista level course (not certified yet but on my way to do so).  If you are looking for Chiang Mai grown coffee this is one of the cool places for that. The Dirty Coffee is a must try to order when you are there. user_reviews.Name: Wasana Tricherdlap
user_reviews.Description:
A café with a wide range of creative menu items, and everything tastes great. The space is large, with a raw loft-style, industrial vibe. There are multiple seating zones on both the first and second floors, and several restrooms available.

The highlight is the outdoor seating area by the Ping River—perfect for relaxing and enjoying the view, especially when the weather isn’t too hot. You can easily sit and chill there for hours. I really like it.

The café offers a variety of drinks, bakery items, and food. The coffee is good, and I also tried another drink (can’t recall the name) that had a nicely balanced blend of flavors. The lemon cake was slightly on the dry side, but the ham & cheese croissant is a must-try—highly recommended, it’s delicious.

There’s parking available in front of the café. You can order at the counter and choose your seat freely. The staff are friendly and provide great service.

user_reviews.Name: Sutrisno Yao
user_reviews.Description:
The Baristro x Ping River is a masterclass in blending industrial design with the natural serenity of Chiang Mai’s riverfront. From the moment you step inside, the raw concrete walls and minimalist wooden accents create an atmosphere that feels both modern and incredibly welcoming. The expansive glass windows offer a stunning view of the Ping River, making it the perfect sanctuary to escape the heat of the city. I found the ambiance to be truly exceptional, especially with the way the sunlight filters through the space during the afternoon.
The coffee here is clearly handled with expert precision, showcasing a depth of flavor that only a dedicated roastery can achieve. Whether you prefer a bold espresso or a creamy latte, the quality of the beans shines through in every single sip. However, the true standout of the visit had to be the tiramisu, which was executed to perfection. It struck the ideal balance between the bitterness of the coffee-soaked layers and the airy sweetness of the mascarpone cream. Every bite was indulgent without being overwhelming, making it one of the best desserts I’ve had in the region. Between the scenic riverside seating and the high-end menu, it is easily a highlight of the Chiang Mai cafe scene. It is the kind of place where you can lose track of time just watching the water flow while enjoying a world-class treat. I would highly recommend this spot to anyone who appreciates great design as much as they do a professional-grade brew.

user_reviews.Name: TheEmpurpler
user_reviews.Description:
We have been here twice now and there are so many good things about this cafe - it is definitely in my top 2 favorite cafes in Chiang Mai!

1) FOOD: all the beverages & snacks we ate so far have been YUMMY. I esp like the soft latte (like a light latte with ice cream & whipped cream) & absolutely LOVE their scones with clotted cream & jam. The scone is a small cute little pastry, paired with a real clotted cream (like from a real tea service, not just butter.)

2) SERVICE: their staff work very quickly & efficiently to bring you what you ordered by using the tabletop number signage, there are many people working to deliver orders & clear tables, and most importantly the staff are friendly, helpful, & customer service oriented. For example, we had a little snafu or misunderstanding with our order (which was easily just as much our fault with our communication!) but they were so apologetic & accommodating in trying to make up for the misunderstanding, even when we insisted we were the ones who made a mistake while ordering! Then they tried to refund some of our money! (We did not take it & insisted they please put it in their tip box!) Lovely!

3) ATMOSPHERE: the view & ambiance are lovely - scenic water, lush trees, many indoor & outdoor areas, plus a variety of seating options- lounge chairs, couches, arm chairs, tables & chairs in a quiet room if you want a work space, etc. (Plus, many of the staff were willing to help take photos since many of their seats are scenic with a view!)

HIGHLY RECOMMEND THIS PLACE! 👍

user_reviews.Name: Living FREE With DEE
user_reviews.Description:
Krisp Café is such a beautiful and peaceful spot.
I ordered the pistachio raspberry croissant, and it was absolutely delicious—perfectly flaky, warm, and rich with buttery layers. The raspberry tasted fresh and added just the right balance without being too sweet. The combination was surprisingly perfect.
I also had a caramel macchiato, which was smooth and well-balanced. No complaints at all.
The best part is the atmosphere. The space is calm, beautifully designed, and offers both open seating and quiet corners if you just want to relax or think. I could easily see myself hosting a small event here or simply coming back for a quiet moment alone.
Highly recommend if you’re in Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Name: Wasana Tricherdlap
user_reviews.Description:
Krisp feels like a hidden gem tucked away in a small alley.
It’s a café with a wide variety of desserts, along with a dedicated baking area.

The Coconut Americano and Dirty were both good and up to standard.
The Chocolate Matcha Lava was especially delicious—the lava combines chocolate and matcha, though the matcha flavor is a bit subtle. Still, it’s well-balanced overall.

The café has three floors, with seating zones uniquely designed on each level. Outside, there’s an old swimming pool repurposed as a photo spot for customers.

The staff are friendly and provide great service. Parking is available along nearby streets.

user_reviews.Name: Athira Mazli
user_reviews.Description:
Roastery Coffee, Chiang Mai

A must-visit for coffee lovers in Chiang Mai! Here’s why:

* 🏆 The baristas are exceptionally skilled, and it’s home to a World Champion Latte Art barista, making every cup feel extra special.
* 😊 The service is warm, friendly, and professional. The staff are happy to answer questions and recommend drinks based on your preferences.
* ☕ The coffee is outstanding, with beautifully crafted espresso drinks and excellent bean quality. Definitely one of the top specialty coffee spots in Chiang Mai.
* 🌿 The café has a comfortable and inviting atmosphere—perfect for relaxing, catching up with friends, or simply enjoying a great cup of coffee.
* 📍 Conveniently located in the heart of the Nimman area, just about a 5-minute walk from One Nimman, making it an easy stop while exploring the neighbourhood.
* 🚕 Parking can be limited, so I would recommend taking Grab for a hassle-free visit.

If you’re serious about specialty coffee or simply want to experience one of Chiang Mai’s best cafés, Roastery Coffee is definitely worth adding to your itinerary.

user_reviews.Name: Kristina Reyes
user_reviews.Description:
Made sure to leave some space for proper coffee after a hearty breakfast elsewhere. Roast8ry was part of our first-order-of-business stops in Chiang Mai. Had a ristretto flat white (which, even in its simplicity, could still go wrong in most coffee shops) and a long black for a grand total of only THB190. This would easily have set us back THB300 or more in Bangkok.

I also particularly love the laid back vibe in their outdoor seating area. Trees, copper chairs that were surprisingly comfortable, and just the right amount of ambient noise from the music and the street. Definitely worth the stop, every single day!

user_reviews.Name: Thanaporn Chote (Newya)
user_reviews.Description:
I’ve been to 7 Senses Gelato many times, and it’s one of those places that I always find myself coming back to. 🍨 The shop offers a wide selection of flavors, from classic options to creative seasonal ones. Every time I visit, I try to discover a new favorite, though I have to admit that most of the flavors are quite sweet for my personal taste since I don’t eat much sugar. However, my company — whether my friend or boyfriend — always enjoys them a lot, so it’s a great spot to share something sweet together.

The shop provides free drinking water, which I find very thoughtful, especially after eating gelato. The staff are a bit shy but always kind, polite, and ready to help. The atmosphere is peaceful and quiet, perfect for sitting down to enjoy a slow afternoon in Chiang Mai.

The location is convenient but not ideal for car parking since the street is quite small; however, it’s easy to park a motorbike nearby. I usually order one or two scoops each visit.

Overall, it’s a charming little gelato shop that serves great flavors with a friendly vibe. Definitely recommended!

user_reviews.Name: Anc
user_reviews.Description:
The indoor area is quite small. If there's a large group of customers, you're most likely going to need to take turns playing with the cats.

And if you happen to arrive at a time when the cats are all sleeping, well, then, probably best just spend time playing some board games provided for free.

None of the cats I observed were curious with the humans, except when they're bribed with food (not kibbles laying on their regular bowls). 90% were sleeping, or hiding away at a corner. Most are ok with petting, but they mostly mind their own business and dgaf about visitors (I suppose they've grown weary of strangers and just acted naturally?)

Also, with the small space and some 10+ cats, there's bound to be a smell. Those that claim there's no smell probably have been living with cats all along, or spent more than 30+ mins inside. It's pronounced when one just steps into it and the smell will integrate with your senses once you're in it long enough. The smell is not that bad though.

The drinks are a little expensive, but they don't charge any other fees so it's reasonable.

I just found it rather boring tbh.

user_reviews.Description:
KLĀY cafe is a beautiful, ambient cafe in the Nimman area which is perfect for a lazy weekend brunch. They have an extremely extensive menu, with many different food and drinks options. It is probably hard to find anywhere else with such a large drink menu — ranging from protein smoothies and fruit juices, to matcha, coffee and tea.

Food wise, we generally enjoyed the food. Our grilled chicken was served a bit raw, but the staff gladly swapped it to a new portion for us. The french toast, pasta and salads were all good and tasty!

Service from the staff was friendly, warm and welcoming as well. There are many other interesting places near the cafe, such as good coffee spots, boutique accessories and the white market/One Nimman Mall. Overall, this is a great place for a date or gathering with friends & family!

user_reviews.Name: liping gan
user_reviews.Description:
KLAY Café is such a beautiful hidden gem in Chiang Mai. The moment you step in, you’ll feel the calm, minimalist vibe — warm wood tones, natural textures, soft lighting, and thoughtful interior design that makes the whole space feel cozy yet modern. It’s the kind of café where you just naturally slow down and enjoy your meal.

We tried a few dishes and everything was beautifully plated and full of flavour:

Smoked Salmon & Eggs Toast
The toast was soft and buttery, topped with generous slices of fresh salmon and perfectly runny eggs. The mix of pickles, tomatoes, and passionfruit on the side added a bright, refreshing balance. Loved how satisfying yet light it was.

Thai Beef Salad
A colourful bowl with tender slices of beef, sweet oranges, juicy tomatoes, red onions, and a nice kick from fresh chili. It’s refreshing with a nice balance of sweet, tangy, and mildly spicy — great for brunch or a hot day.

Besides the food, the café also has a small curated retail corner with skincare and lifestyle products, adding a boutique feel to the place. It’s a lovely spot for brunch, a slow afternoon coffee, or even just to chill and enjoy the aesthetic environment.

Overall, KLAY Café is definitely worth a visit if you’re in Chiang Mai — delicious food, beautiful ambience, and a very inviting atmosphere.

title: Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store
address: 24, Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store, 9 Nimmanhaemin Soi 17, Suthep, Muang, Chiang Mai 50200
plus_code: QXV9+X9 Chiang Mai, Mueang Chiang Mai District, Chiang Mai

user_reviews.Name: Tyler
user_reviews.Description:
If you’re serious about coffee, Roast8ry Coffee Flagship Store is a must-visit in Chiang Mai. This place completely lived up to the hype for us. From the moment you walk in, you can tell coffee is taken very seriously here — the space feels modern, stylish, and almost like a specialty coffee lab rather than just a café.

The coffee itself was incredible. Smooth, rich, perfectly balanced, and easily some of the best coffee we had in Thailand. You can really tell why Roast8ry has become internationally known in the coffee world, especially with their award-winning baristas and latte art. Watching the drinks being made honestly felt like part of the experience itself. (Food & Wine)

We also loved the atmosphere. The dark modern interior, the smell of freshly roasted beans, the music, and the overall energy made it somewhere we genuinely wanted to stay for a while instead of just grabbing a coffee and leaving. It felt trendy without trying too hard.

It’s located in the Nimman area which is already one of the best neighborhoods in Chiang Mai for cafés and restaurants, so it fits perfectly into a café hopping day around the city. Prices are definitely higher than local Thai coffee shops, but for the quality and experience, it was absolutely worth it.

If you enjoy specialty coffee even a little bit, Roast8ry Flagship Store is one of those places in Chiang Mai that you should not skip.

plus_code: PWPJ+F8 Nong Kwai, Hang Dong District, Chiang Mai

user_reviews.Name: Syrristen
user_reviews.Description:
Delicous food, great service and fantastic vibes!

The food was great. It was very well made, came quickly and tasted just like it was supposed to. Both drinks and food were very profesionally made. It was a little but pricey compared to other places, but it's a very touristy place and there's a lot of upkeep with the fish, so it's understandable.

The service was terrific! We were serviced quickly and when ready to order they came immediately. The waiters were very kind, patient and seemed happy to be at work.

And of course, the venue! It was so cool with all the fish, and the seats were inside of the pool, under waterlevel, so that you could easily see, feed and interact with the hundreds of fishes there. Ask for fish food and you will get 2 choices; normal fish food or a baby bottle so you can feed them like a baby.

The whole experience was really fun and I recommend you try it when you're in town 😄

user_reviews.Name: Ardila Ayob
user_reviews.Description:
A koi carp café with an outstanding and unique design. The concept is beautiful and very eye-catching, making it a great place to explore and take photos.

You can feed the fish by purchasing fish pellets and fish milk provided by the café. One of the highlights is the uniquely designed toilet area filled with koi fish — it’s definitely something you should check out when you visit.

The overall atmosphere is nice and relaxing. However, there is room for improvement in terms of indoor odor. It seems to be affected by humidity, fish smell, and a slightly musty scent from the seating materials, which can make the experience a bit uncomfortable at times.

Hopefully, the management can look into improving this issue, as the café has great potential with its creative concept and design.

user_reviews.Description:
A beautiful café with such a peaceful atmosphere! The setting is unique—you can enjoy your meal inside a circular seating area surrounded by water, making the whole experience feel relaxing and close to nature. For a small fee, you can buy fish food and feed the fish in the pond. As soon as you throw the food into the water, hundreds of fish rush over, which is surprisingly fun to watch.

The food was delicious, very reasonably priced (even on the cheaper side compared to many cafés we visited), and the natural surroundings made the experience even better. If you're looking for a relaxing spot with great views, affordable food, and a unique atmosphere in Chiang Mai, I highly recommend stopping by!

user_reviews.Name: Robert Haehnel
user_reviews.Description:
The Carp Café in Chiang Mai is definitely worth a visit. The atmosphere is really unique and makes it a great place for a relaxed lunch or dinner. 🐟🌿

The whole place is surrounded by countless koi carp, some of them absolutely huge, swimming right around the seating areas. The café itself shows a little bit of age in a few places, but that really doesn’t matter – you come here for the experience, and that is fantastic.

The food was also very good, and the prices were surprisingly reasonable. I honestly expected it to be much more expensive considering how special the setting is.

If you visit with children, definitely buy some fish food for 20 baht – or even better, get one of the feeding bottles for 40 baht. 😄 Feeding the koi with the bottle was a huge hit with the kids and a lot of fun.

Funny enough, it’s even cheaper than doing something similar at Chiang Mai Zoo.

Great atmosphere, good food, fair prices and a really fun experience. Clear recommendation! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Ristr8to Original is a memorable coffee spot in the Nimman area of Chiang Mai, especially if you enjoy specialty coffee and latte art.

The latte art was the highlight, but the coffee itself was also enjoyable — rich, aromatic, and not just pretty for photos. The small snacks and dessert were nice to have on the side, though the coffee is definitely the main reason to come here.

Worth stopping by if you are already exploring Nimman and want a coffee place with personality.

user_reviews.Name: Eugene Bogdanov
user_reviews.Description:
One of the most memorable specialty coffee experiences I've had.
I ordered a V60 brewed with locally grown Thai beans from Chiang Rai. The coffee itself was excellent—clean, sweet, well-balanced, with delicate floral and fruity notes—but what really impressed me was the attention to detail.

The coffee was served in a wine glass with a lid to preserve the aroma, alongside a handwritten brew card showing all the extraction parameters: brew ratio, dose, water temperature, brew time, TDS, and even the expected flavor profile. It felt less like ordering a cup of coffee and more like a personalized tasting experience.

You can tell the team genuinely cares about every step of the process, from sourcing the beans to the final presentation. If you enjoy specialty coffee, MoR is absolutely worth a visit.

This place is very interesting and made me want to learn more about the Thai chocolate industry. It seems to be a rapidly growing industry.
The female staff at the counter explained everything very well – clearly, concisely, and with recommendations based on my preferences, making my selection much easier.
The chocolate shots were rich and delicious, especially the Thai-style one I tried. It was more bitter despite having a similar cocoa percentage, which was very interesting because I usually can't distinguish the difference between chocolate terroirs.
It was a great learning experience.
There seemed to be many tempting pastries, but I had already been to three cafes that day, so I wasn't up for trying any more, haha.
There were cute souvenirs and small sample packs available for purchase.

user_reviews.Name: Gönpo
user_reviews.Description:
We are always on the lookout for great coffee and authenticity. You definitely can find that here. I’ve had a lot of coffee in my life but this is the first time I’ve had farm to table.

Pim, the owner and farmer, happened to be in the shop and made two wonderful coffees for us. Despite her costs doubling over the last few years she’s kept her ristretto, espresso and doppio at 50 THB.

If you’re into coffee, you have to give the place a try. Btw, there is a great wine bar, Cru, across the street.

Pim recommended visiting the nearby night market as well as Wat Phra Singh to catch the sunset behind the gold stupa.

user_reviews.reply_text_original:
Hi Kunal, thank you for the review! You hit the nail on the head—we prioritize the bean over the 'vibes.'
​Coffee is our life's blood. We spend a lot of our time in the mountains of Northern Thailand (like Doi Saket and Mae Jan Tai), working side-by-side with local farmers. We help select the cherries ourselves because we believe the best coffee starts with the soil and the hard work of the people growing it.
​By keeping our shop simple, we make sure nothing distracts you from the natural flavors we’ve worked so hard to bring from the farm to your cup. We’re thrilled that the balance of our dirty coffee showed you exactly what we’re about.
​See you again soon for another serious brew!"

user_reviews.Name: SamantaMiki
user_reviews.Description: I stayed here for 10 nights and chose it mostly because its located at a walking distance from the Night Bazaar, the Wat Chedi Luang (a 10 to 15 min. walk to both) and because of the price - it was quite hard to find a non-shared room for less than USD 15, especially an a/c one, very much needed in Chiang Mai.||I got the Superior Room - No Balcony, but upgraded to the one with balcony for less than a couple dollars per night. They gave me a discount because I had a long stay here. Both rooms are small indeed, but I found them comfortable enough. There's a double bed with a firm-but-comfortable mattress, nice pillows and comforter, a small bedside table, cable flat screen TV, and two 0.5L complimentary bottles of water per night. The bathroom is also small but it's not cramped. The water is hot (you can adjust the temperature), the water pressure is good and the towels are big. The a/c works pretty well.||The staff is friendly and kind. Their youngest "staff, Minah, is such a pretty, well behaved and cute little girl! It's a very homey feeling you get here. They provide laundry service at 40 baht/kg and will clean the room upon request. There's indeed a lot of mosquitoes, but I suppose you can just ask for a bug spray. I managed to kill the ones in my room on the first night and didn't get any more uninvited visitors. There's no elevator here and the rooms are located on the 3rd and 4th floor. I also got a 1h foot scrub with massage for THB 350 and it was very good. The sir who did it has a very firm grip, which I prefer and not only my foot and calf are soft and smooth, but the calf pain I was feeling after so much walking is gone!||There's plenty of B&Bs and restaurants on the street where F.K. House is located to have meals. I recommend Da's Home Bakery for their Mixed fruit with Muesli and Yogurt, Addy's Happy Smoothies for their Iced Thai Milk Tea and Iced Coffee Milk, and Lucky Too for their pizzas.||Right on the corner it's Somphet Fresh Food market where, apart from fruit and vegetables, you can buy BBQed meat and fish, small trays of sliced fruits (10 to 20 baht), fruit shakes (40 baht) and some souvenirs - good to have an idea of starting prices before going to the other famous markets. Within 100m you can find a Tesco Lotus Express, a 7-Eleven, ATM, drugstores and local restaurants. I recommend Grazie Thai, I had so many meals there and the dishes are very tasty! I also tried Aroy Dee but for me it was just okay.||For the price, comfort, and location, I'd say it's a great deal!

Nestled on the top floor of the building, away from the bustling streets of Nimman, is FOHHIDE. They have a good variety of coffee drinks and mixes, which is nice, but what the place truly delivers is the experience that comes with it.

The view looks directly towards Doi Suthep, over the rooftops of Nimman, with planes flying by; all from the comfort of an air-conditioned café. In fact, on a good day where clouds are thinner, you may even spot Wat Phra That Doi Suthep.

Best of all, they accept Apple Pay/card and mobile payments without any extra charge (as I write this), and the coffee is pretty well priced. I found myself coming back multiple times over the next few days.

user_reviews.Description:
FOHHIDE is truly a hidden gem, tucked away on a building in the heart of Nimmanhaemin. It’s a small, charming café where you can enjoy a great view of Chiang Mai city. The staff are friendly and welcoming.

The café offers drinks and bakery items, and most of the seating is bar-style—either at the counter or at the bar facing the view. The coffee is excellent.

There are both indoor and outdoor seating areas. The outdoor section is especially popular, as many people come there to take photos. It’s definitely a must-visit spot to check in when you’re in Chiang Mai.

Sincerely wish this lovely family‑owned restaurant ongoing prosperity. I truly encourage travellers to come and experience its heart‑warming charm for themselves.

user_reviews.Name: Lola Forsan
user_reviews.Description:
🍰☕ This café is more than just a coffee shop, everything feels truly homemade. From the freshly baked pastries with their delightful aroma to the drinks crafted with care, it’s like having something made by a family member just for you.

The atmosphere is cozy and heartwarming. The decor is simple yet charming, with wooden tables,flowers, and soft sunlight streaming in. It feels like sitting in a friend’s living room. It’s a perfect spot to relax, get some work done, or enjoy a chat with friends.

The cakes and pastries are baked fresh daily, with just the right sweetness, reminiscent of recipes you’d taste at home. The coffee and drinks are rich and aromatic (not to sweet). Best of all, the owners and their family are so kind and welcoming, making you feel right at home every time you visit.

Overall, it’s a small but charming café full of warmth and character — perfect for anyone looking for a little hideaway with genuine homemade treats. 🏡💛

user_reviews.Name: David Devlim
user_reviews.Description:
Blue Coffee at Agriculture CMU is a hidden gem tucked into the Faculty of Agriculture at Chiang Mai University. This spacious cafe boasts stunning glass walls, high ceilings, and wooden accents that create a warm, modern farmhouse vibe, all while overlooking experimental agricultural fields and greenery.
It's the perfect blend of cafe and co-working space—ideal for students, digital nomads, or anyone seeking a peaceful spot to sip specialty coffee, study, or relax. The drinks, from The Baristro brand, feature standout artisanal roasts and creative specials in a serene, nature-inspired setting.
Highly recommended for its photogenic interior, lovely views, and productive atmosphere. A must-visit if you're near CMU!

user_reviews.Name: Koravit Thummanond
user_reviews.Description:
Lot of Taste, better known as L.O.T., is a specialty coffee café in Chiang Mai's Nimman area. Designed with a minimalist blend of exposed concrete and warm wood, the space feels open, bright, and relaxing thanks to the abundance of natural light. Rather than being a café built purely for Instagram, it is a place where people come to enjoy good coffee. One of its highlights is the variety of coffee beans available, along with its signature drinks featuring Soft Cream, which gives the café a unique identity beyond a typical latte.

When I visited, the café was quite busy with a mix of locals, tourists, and expats. Some were working on their laptops while others were catching up with friends, yet the atmosphere remained calm and comfortable.

Here's what I tried:

Hot Latte
The café uses its own house blend, combining beans from Doi Chang and Lator Gold. The result is a balanced cup with smooth milk, gentle acidity, low bitterness, a creamy texture, and subtle caramel sweetness. It's easy to drink and well-rounded without being overpowering.

Soft Latte
This is the café's signature drink and one that many people come specifically to try. Instead of traditional milk foam, it's topped with a thick layer of Soft Cream, similar in texture to soft serve, sitting on an iced latte. Each spoonful gives you both coffee and cream together. The Soft Cream is silky and lightly sweet—lighter than whipped cream and far less sugary than ice cream. It's worth tasting the cream on its own first before gently stirring it into the coffee, as the flavor gradually changes from the first sip to the last.

Tiramisu
The tiramisu has a light, airy texture with just the right amount of sweetness. It pairs naturally with coffee without feeling too rich, and melts smoothly in your mouth.

If you're exploring Nimman and looking for a comfortable place to relax with a well-made cup of coffee and a slice of dessert, Lot of Taste is definitely a café worth adding to your list.

user_reviews.Name: Athira Mazli
user_reviews.Description:
Lot of Taste Coffee, Chiang Mai

Visited this lovely café at One Nimman and had a great experience! Here are my thoughts:

* 📍 Located in the heart of One Nimman, making it a very convenient stop while exploring the area.
* 🕗 Open daily from 8:00am to 10:00pm.
* ☕ The baristas are incredibly friendly, warm, and knowledgeable. They’re happy to recommend coffees based on your preferences.
* 🌱 They offer a wide selection of coffee and matcha drinks.
* 🫘 They roast their own coffee beans, and you can also purchase their freshly roasted beans to take home.
* 🍰 They have a selection of desserts that pair perfectly with their coffee.
* 🪑 The café is very spacious, quiet, and relaxing, with soft jazz playing in the background—perfect for winding down after a day of sightseeing.
* 👨‍👩‍👧 Great for tourists looking to unwind, or for parents who want to relax while the rest of the family explores the lively atmosphere of One Nimman, especially in the evening.
* 🚕 I’d recommend taking Grab, as parking around One Nimman can be busy.

A wonderful specialty coffee spot with excellent coffee, welcoming service, and a peaceful atmosphere. Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Chiang Mai!

user_reviews.Description:
A much overrated place.

I first tried their cloud latte (130baht). It was simply an iced latte made from decent doi Chang coffee bean, with a low-quality coconut ice cream on top. And both elements had zero synergy in flavors.

Later i decided it to give it a second try since it features quite a few very interesting beans. I ordered a passion-fruit-fermented black (120baht). As opposed to most fruit-enzyme-processed bean which taste exceptionally fruity and characteristic of the fruit used, it was average at best.

And the barista in the afternoon and night gave me different info about their coffee, which is not a sign of well-trained staff.

At a higher-end price in Chiang Mai, this does not meet the cut.

강바람 맞으면서 고양이 쓰다듬을 수 있는 평화로운 카페입니다. 🌿🐱

The scenery here is absolutely beautiful, making it the perfect place to relax and enjoy some peaceful time looking out over the Ping River. Even though there is no air conditioning, the natural river breeze keeps the place pleasantly cool.

The lychee tea in my photo not only looks beautiful but tastes amazing. The honey lemon tea I had the day before was also delicious, and they even refilled it with hot water. They serve decent meals and desserts like Basque cheesecake. There is a Halal sign, so dishes like Pad Kra Pao are available only with chicken or beef. There are also lovely resident cats here, and you can buy cat treats for 20 THB to feed them. Free Wi-Fi is available as well.

I would absolutely love to come back here the next time I visit Chiang Mai. Thank you for such a wonderful experience! 🙏✨

user_reviews.Description:
Cocoa Latte 70 ฿ (2026)

Has English menu.

A hidden gem!!

Just look at the view, and the greens in the cafe, they are so relaxing and beautiful.

The owner/staff very friendly and smiling. It gives good vibe.

There are many different types of seating and the design is very good as not cramp so it won’t get noisy.

And the Ping river is the main protagonist, peaceful, calm, murky.

And the sun, best supporting actor of all time, shining thru the trees on my seat, on the river, making it glistening from time to time.

And best cameo goes to occasional boat passing by, making ripples, just like witnessing time passing in slow motion and dance right in front of my eyes.

I stare at it for the longest time, while enjoying my coffee, didn’t realize time passing in un relative sense.

I had my AirPod on, with Debussy playing for me, this could be one of the best moment that I need to remember how wonderful to be alive.

I am just another ordinary human, quietly living, but I awed at my blessing, the beauty of my surroundings.

The feeling is wonderful.

And I wish you could feel that too.

user_reviews.Name: Michael McElligott
user_reviews.Description:
This is my favorite little “hidden gem” coffee shop in Chiang Mai. Super-friendly owners, amazing coffee and non-coffee drinks (their Thai iced tea was one of the best I had in Thailand), and some tasty pastries to go along with it!  They sell some fantastic local beans as well, which I can highly recommend. For the quality, it’s amazing how reasonable the prices are.

When the weather is moderate they open up the front of the shop to be open-air, but during the heat of the afternoon they close it to keep it nice and cool inside with air conditioning. Very convenient location to grab-and-go, but they have a surprising large amount of seating for such a tiny little place: 2-3 benches/tables inside, as well as 3 tables outside. Really recommend for a getting a drink and people-watching for a wee bit outside.

Edit (August 2025): Was back in Chiang Mai and wanted to stop in again. The shop has changed a bit and become better! They had added a much larger indoor seating area (you can comfortably sit with your drink), and they also have a list of single origin and house blend coffee beans you can choose from to have as a pour-over or in your coffee drink of choice. I am adding the pictures below to show these changes. They’ve also got a few more creative coffee concoction, as well as some desserts (cookies and cheesecake) to choose from. user_reviews.Name: Badro Badreddine Mimouni
user_reviews.Description:
12 Feb Homey Café is a peaceful, beautifully designed spot in Chiang Mai.

The building is calm and minimalist, with a Japanese feel: a stone path through raked gravel, a neat green lawn and a simple house with floor-to-ceiling windows. Inside, light wood, soft white curtains and comfortable chairs make it bright and relaxing, with garden views from every table.

We had the yogurt bowls, topped with fresh orange, banana, apple, grapes, blueberries and granola, served with honey and extra toppings on the side. The thick toast came with butter and a lovely homemade orange marmalade, and the Thai iced tea was a good match. Simple, fresh and nicely presented, with real attention to detail.

A perfect place for a slow breakfast, a quiet coffee or a few hours of reading. Highly recommended.

12FEB Homey Cafe is an absolute gem of a spot, offering a serene, homey atmosphere surrounded by lush greenery and open lawns. The entire space is designed with a warm, minimalist wooden style, with large windows that let in soft natural light, making it feel calm and inviting from the moment you walk in. The sprawling outdoor garden is full of well-maintained grass, leafy trees, and quiet corners, perfect for relaxing, reading, or simply enjoying the breeze. The cafe itself is clean and spacious, with a light, airy interior that blends seamlessly with the natural surroundings. I loved wandering around the grounds, taking in the peaceful vibe, and the quiet atmosphere makes it ideal for both working and unwinding. Whether you’re here for coffee or just to soak up the calm, this spot is a perfect escape from the busy city center. Highly recommend visiting if you’re looking for a tranquil, nature-filled cafe experience in Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Name: Joel Horowitz
user_reviews.Description:
intensely into drip coffee,  per much of the new coffee culture here. Ordering a drip coffee here is having a voyeuristic adventure.  They don't do big brew baskets/pots of coffee . Drip coffee means a personalized, experienced, individual coffee. Every step of the process, which u r invited to see upclose is meticulously crafted and cured . Weighed carefully, ground by hand grinder, sniffed for perfection, poured in cool genie bottle glass (similar to ChemEx), then poured back n forth from different glasses to achieve maximum taste by not letting it get too hot.  It was amazing . Coffee was too 😄.   They only do light roast or similar of course. Max flavor profiles.  Notice the light hue of the coffee.
The whole place is like a retro flappers era bar, cool music ,  odd statue carving stores in the back through the narrow hall.
Lots of hip Thai young people there.
Highly recommend for coffee snobs. They take coffee extremely serious . (Discourage milk or cream ofc, but they'll give u milk if u want on the side).
And also , see how they make iced coffee !! They pour hot pour over into a bowl of ice 🧊!😮, which is apparently popular here

user_reviews.Description:
We were staying at theOmbra small house no. 3 above the Ombra Caffe for 4 days in Jan 2026.  As there is no google pin for the house, I would like to leave the review of the house and caffe here.  We had an absolutely fantastic stay at The Ombra Small House No. 3 in Chiang Mai! From the moment I booked, Jennie was super helpful and responsive — she replied to my messages lightning fast, provided very clear check-in instructions and went above and beyond to assist with anything I needed. She was super proactive too, even recommending some great nearby food spots that I ended up loving.
We were staying at theguest house of Ombra Caffe upstairs.  As there is no google pin for the guest house, Iwould like to leave my review of the house and the cafe here.  The house itself is incredibly spacious — perfect for relaxing. It’s super super clean; even when I walked around barefoot without the provided slippers, the floor felt spotless with zero dust at all. The bed is comfortable — I slept so well every night! There’s a smart TV with Netflix and the place is very well-equipped with everything you could need (kitchenette, fridge, etc.).
Downstairs there’s their Ombra Cafe (which you can store your luggage before and after check-out). I believe they can deliver food up to the room (though I didn’t try it this time, I went down to eat and the food was great!
Overall, this place exceeded all my expectations. Next time I’m in Chiang Mai, I will definitely stay here again without hesitation. Highly highly recommended — you won’t be disappointed! Thank you Jennie and the team!

user_reviews.Name: Juztin Png
user_reviews.Description:
Tucked within One Nimman, GRAPH Coffee is such a delightful spot to unwind. The environment is beautiful—cozy, stylish, and very inviting. It’s the kind of place where you can easily lose track of time just enjoying the atmosphere.

What really stands out is their extensive selection of coffee mocktails. These are not your usual drinks—each one is a unique and creative blend, mixing coffee with unexpected flavors. Truly impressive and exciting for any coffee lover.

We ordered the Downtown, and wow, it was incredibly refreshing and tasted soooo good! Perfect for the summer heat. Honestly, it was so addictive I was tempted to go for a second cup immediately.

My friend had the Jungle, which leans towards a more earthy profile, paired with their signature soda mix. A really interesting and exotic take on coffee—great for those who enjoy something a little different.

The croffle was another highlight—crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and absolutely satisfying as a light bite. They also offer a good selection of pastries if you’re looking for something to go along with your drinks.

Overall, a fantastic experience with great drinks, cozy vibes, and creative offerings.
Highly recommended!

user_reviews.Name: Daniyal Saleem
user_reviews.Description:
A beautiful hidden gem and one of those places where you can easily lose track of time. This boutique café has a cozy, peaceful atmosphere with lots of character. The upstairs area is especially calm and quiet, making it a great spot to get some work done, read, or simply relax with a good cup of coffee.

What makes the place unique is the beautiful collection of handcrafted wooden items throughout the boutique, from chopsticks and ladles to photo frames and decorative pieces. The interior and wall décor add even more charm, while the large windows offer a lovely view—especially on a rainy afternoon. ☕️🌧️

The coffee is excellent, with espresso-based drinks made using beans ranging from light to dark roasts. I tried the Thai local medium roast, which had a smooth, medium body with pleasant nutty notes. The pastries and desserts are also worth trying—the banana croffle and mango sticky rice were beautifully presented and delicious.

Overall, it’s a wonderful place to spend a couple of hours browsing the handcrafted items, enjoying coffee and pastries, or getting some work done in a peaceful setting. Highly recommended! ☕️✨

user_reviews.Name: feisal permana
user_reviews.Description: Kurokuro Coffee Roaster is an absolute gem that manages to be both incredibly "cute" and serious about its craft. The interior is charmingly designed, but the real magic is in the backyard, there’s a comfortable outdoor sitting area right by the canal that feels like a private escape from the world. I highly recommend their Dirty Coffee; it’s exceptionally well-balanced and easily some of the best I’ve had. To top it all off, their resident cat is adorable and adds a lovely, homey vibe to the place. It’s the perfect spot to lose an hour or two with a cold drink and a view of the water.

user_reviews.Name: Yassir El Ghazi
user_reviews.Description:
Some places serve great coffee and cake. Others leave you with a beautiful memory. TORA BAKE somehow manages to do both. ❤️

I genuinely had such a wonderful time here. The food and drinks were delicious, and I especially recommend the chocolate mint cake! Everything feels carefully made, with love and attention to detail. I also really appreciate their eco-friendly, zero-waste philosophy. It's lovely to see a small business that genuinely cares about these things.

The café itself is peaceful, cozy and welcoming. Whether you want to read a book, enjoy a coffee, get some work done or rent a dedicated workspace, it's a wonderful little escape from the busy city.

But what truly makes TORA BAKE special is Ice, the owner.

What an incredibly kind, warm and genuine person. We had such a lovely conversation, and honestly, that human connection was the highlight of my visit. She has this beautiful way of making you feel welcome, not just as a customer, but as a person. You can find good coffee, delicious cakes and coworking spaces in many places in Chiang Mai, but the warmth and positive energy Ice brings to this little café are something you simply can't replicate.

As a traveler, these are the moments I value most. Sometimes you walk into a place expecting nothing more than a nice drink, and you leave with a smile, a meaningful conversation and a memory you'll carry with you.

Thank you, Ice, for your kindness, your beautiful energy and for making my time here so special. I wish you and TORA BAKE all the success and happiness you deserve! ❤️

If you're visiting Chiang Mai, please don't miss this little gem. And when you go, make sure to say hello to Ice for me! 😊

I'll definitely remember this place long after leaving Chiang Mai. Will be back for sure Ice :)

This café has officially become my favorite coffee spot in Chiang Mai — almost my little secret that I hesitate to share.

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a peaceful and high-quality coffee experience in Chiang Mai.

They have a large selection of drinks available, and a fine display of cakes and other sweets. They have AC, and a cool industrial feel on the inside.

We ordered a Blue Latte and a Cold Brew Cream. They were both really good, and probably worth the total cost of 210 Baht, which is the most we've paid for coffee in the area.

The staff was friendly, and brought our drinks to our table when they were ready. Overall it was a good experience, and we would be happy to return.

user_reviews.Name: Courtney McCarthy
user_reviews.Description:
150 baht per person to enter and it comes with a free drink. There is a place to hang up your bags and they ask that you either bring socks, or tell provide you with a pair of you can buy snacks for the kitties, too.

There has to be like 20 cats in this cafe. It was soooo clean, and the cats are so cute and friendly. When you order a drink, it comes with a cover on it so no fur gets in. Fur is everywhere haha. They let you hold them, you just need to be sitting down. They have two floors, and there are cats everywhere you look. This was such a fun time, you get to stay for two hours. Right outside is a little market, there’s a restaurant and there’s a cafe and juice shop as well. They even had live music when we arrived.

If you bring a car, you can park for 50 baht. I’d recommend coming not only to the cat cafe, but check out the vendors, the food and art stores around as well. A cute little gem, hidden and tucked away. Definitely a great place to bring family if they’re visiting.

If you bring a car, you can park for 50 baht. I’d recommend coming not only to the cat cafe, but check out the vendors, the food and art stores around as well. A cute little gem, hidden and tucked away. Definitely a great place to bring family if they’re visiting.

user_reviews.Name: Conita Ng
user_reviews.Description:
A cozy Cat Cafe,  just 5 mins walk from art village Baan Kang Wat.  Visitors need to wash hands and wear socks before getting inside.  THB 150 per person for a 2-hour session with a nice drink.  Staff informed us some rules about how to get along well with cats such as hanging up bags, put lids on our drinks, and no holding cats moving around, etc.  We can see how they take care of visitors and cats by setting up clear rules.
There are over 20 friendly cats napping or enjoying their time around.  After a while sitting quietly with them, a few may approach you and even jump on your thigh purring.
As a cat lover, I love this place and definitely will come again next time when we visit Chiang Mai.

user_reviews.Name: OcP_Fact finder_Info Sharer
user_reviews.Description:
Late January 2026 Local Hmong cafe serving a wide range of specialty and crafted coffee ☕️

One of the few interesting places at the village originated when the peoples of this region once cultivated opium poppy plantations.  The then late king made efforts to introduce more sustainable alternative crops and soon a small coffee industry was born.

The selection itself is notable from basic blends to single origin beans 🫘 reflecting the deep knowledge of the family behind this local brand.  Even selective beans are available as well as various brewing options.

The staff is strictly counter style with option to do your own pour 🫗 over order.  Retails options are also available as well as other coffee by products and alternative drinks.  Meals pairings are also at hand.

The atmosphere and the view are particularly beautiful and once can imagine the restful view in the early sunrises 🌅 😍 👌   Truly one of the must visit places in the village.

user_reviews.Name: sheetha iam
user_reviews.Description:
Visited with a large group of friends and ordered several drinks, desserts, and ice cream. Overall, the café is lovely, the atmosphere is great, and the matcha was absolutely delicious.

The only issue we experienced was with the service. One of our drinks was ordered hot but was served cold. When we politely informed the staff, we were told that we had not specified that we wanted it hot. However, the person who placed the order had actually asked which drinks could be served hot before ordering, so we were quite confident that the request had been made.

What was disappointing was not the mistake itself, as errors can happen anywhere, but the response and attitude we received. The staff member seemed visibly annoyed and unwilling to acknowledge that there may have been a misunderstanding.

Thankfully, another staff member stepped in and kindly said, “No problem, we’ll fix it for you,” and resolved the issue right away. We really appreciated her professionalism and helpful attitude.

Mistakes happen, especially when a café is busy, but I believe maintaining a positive attitude and listening to customers carefully is just as important as serving great food and drinks.

Despite this experience, we still enjoyed our visit. The matcha was excellent, the desserts were lovely, and the café itself is beautiful. I hope the team can improve the consistency of their customer service, as the café has so much potential

The prices may seem a bit high for a basic menu, but the taste is reasonable and definitely worth it.

Please don’t give up—keep going and keep improving! You’re one of my favorite places, and I’d love to come back whenever I travel to CNX!

user_reviews.Name: Sercan Çelik
user_reviews.Description:
The Little Cat Cafe is a nice, relaxed spot to spend some time in Chiang Mai. The atmosphere is calm and cozy, and it doesn’t feel too crowded or hectic.

The cats seem well taken care of and mostly just chill around, so you can interact with them but also just sit and enjoy your drink.

The coffee and matcha are good, and they also have some simple bakery options. Prices are fair for what you get.

Overall, it’s a good place if you like cats and want to relax for a bit without anything too fancy.

user_reviews.Name: Kai
user_reviews.Description:
Genuinely a pleasant experience at Box Box Dog Cafe.

The cafe is thoughtfully divided into two sections: a separate play area with the dogs and a cozy seating space for cafe guests. The room has a bright, light ambiance.

As for the dogs, their temperaments range from super chill to very high-energy/rowdy. They don't break anything or pose real harm, but you should still be careful when playing with them, just give the staff a quick nod if the play gets a bit too wild.

A note on pricing/policy: I had read previous reviews mentioning a 500 baht entry fee for foreigners, but after speaking with the owner and seeing it firsthand, that policy has been scrapped. Access is now based simply on purchasing a drink, which makes it much more reasonable and accessible.

user_reviews.Name: Selina Eshraghi
user_reviews.Description:
I almost didn’t post this review since I don’t want to blow up this spot, but after going here multiple times within the two weeks we were in Chiang Mai, I felt like it was my duty to share how magical this place is.

As someone who drinks matcha everyday at home I was craving  quality matcha spot and kohicha is quite literally the best matcha experience I’ve had. Their menu has a wide variety of strains with tasting notes listed as well as a guide to which ones make for good lattes and which are best drank just with water. Oat milk swap is free and there are other alt milk options!

All the staff is really knowledgeable and have great recommendations.

The wifi is great for working and there are a few larger tables and outlets. It does get busy so these spots are not always guaranteed. It’s also a dog friendly location which has been a welcome distraction in my experience.

I’d also highly recommend the daifuku strawberry mochi. I get it every time! The chocolate cake is also phenomenal. The Nutty Yama has been my favorite so far out of the ~10 I’ve tried but it’s also a limited edition option.

Bring cash as card is not accepted.

user_reviews.Name: Artiste, Jet
user_reviews.Description:
We had a wonderful late lunch at Building A Cafe, which shares the same space as ME & BACON Nawarat, and it was such a delightful surprise.

Hidden behind a quiet alley, this charming café offers a peaceful atmosphere that’s perfect for slowing down and enjoying the moment. The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully prepared, while the coffee was excellent—rich, aromatic, and exactly what we needed for a relaxing afternoon.

The crossover between Building A Cafe and ME & BACON Nawarat creates a unique experience, combining a cozy café atmosphere with delicious, satisfying food. The warm, welcoming environment and genuinely friendly service made the visit even more memorable.

If you’re exploring Chiang Mai and looking for a hidden gem with great coffee, excellent food, a relaxing ambiance, and wonderful hospitality, this is definitely a place worth visiting.

user_reviews.Name: Moritz Klauer
user_reviews.Description:
Serene Backyard is a beautiful little nook surrounded by greens right in the center of Chiang Mai. Offering riverside dining and lounging, the hosts provide a very warm and caring atmosphere that makes you want to extend your stay from lunch until dinner time and beyond. They have a great variety of food and drinks that cater to many different tastes. Live music bars are within walking distance and according to the staff there will be concerts at the Serene Backyard in the near future too. No need to change locations if you’re that type of person. All in one well done. Love finding these gems. Hats off to the new team. Keep it up! Cheers

PS: Can't speak for the rooms yet besides the looks, but the accommodation definitely caters to the ones who stay up til closing time anyway as the rooms are more or less above the main area. You just gotta walk up a set of stairs and can go to bed.
